title: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames

summary.text: The E-FIELD Flames investigation studies how electric fields influence laminar diffusion flames of methane and ethylene in microgravity, in the combustion integrated rack.

fuels.text: Methane and ethylene, diluted with nitrogen.

geometry.text: Gas-fueled flames with and without a coflow of air, with a high voltage (up to 10 kV) between the burner and a mesh downstream.

flow.text: Fuel flow rate and coflow velocity were varied.

measurements.text: Voltage-current curves, spectral imaging of chemiluminescence and soot volume fraction, and thermopile radiant emission.

claims.text: The investigation aims to better understand the relationship between electric field voltage and chemi-ion current, analyze the dynamic response of flames to electric field changes, evaluate soot formation, and characterize stabilized near-limit lifted flames.
The investigation hypothesizes that the application of electric fields in microgravity environments will significantly influence laminar diffusion flames.

limitations.text: The source states the research is not being conducted to serve any space applications.
Only PSI metadata was examined; no document text was processed.

modeling_resources.description: Experimental table for the E-FIELD Flames investigation, relevant to voltage-current, imaging and radiant emission measurements.

evidence.excerpt: The objective of this investigation is to better understand the relationship between electric field voltage and chemi-ion current, analyze the dynamic response of flames to electric field changes, evaluate soot formation, and characterize stabilized near-limit lifted flames.
The application of electric fields in microgravity environments will significantly influence laminar diffusion flames
The experiment is conducted with gas-fueled flames, both with and without a coflow of air.
An electric field is generated by creating a high voltage (up to 10 kV) differential between the burner and a flat circular mesh suspended above (i.e., downstream of) the burner.
Methane and ethylene were used as fuels and diluted with nitrogen to control flame strength.
All experiments were conducted in the combustion integrated rack (CIR).
Spectral imaging with filters measures chemiluminescent emissions and soot volume fraction.
There were thermopile detectors to measure flame radiant emissions.
The E-FIELD Flames research is not being conducted to serve any space applications
The E-FIELD flames experiment investigates how electric fields influence the behavior of laminar diffusion flames in microgravity.
Parameters such as fuel flow rate, coflow velocity, and field polarity are were varied
Voltage-current curves were recorded to assess the relationship between electric field strength and chemi-ion current
